rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.9 describe a two-year (2004-2005) field trial in a Cabernet Sauvignon vineyard in Sicily comparing surface drip (DR) with two subsurface drip treatments (SDI 0, SDI 120) in three randomized blocks. Q2: Section 3.6 and Table 5 report yield per vine by treatment; SDI 120 yielded 44% more than DR in 2004 and 49.7% more in 2005, SDI 0 intermediate and not significantly different from DR; Conclusions state subsurface irrigation gave higher production with 20% less water. Q4: Sections 2.2/3.3 and Fig. 1 report predawn leaf water potential as plant water status across treatments (similar despite 20% less water in SDI); Sections 3.5, 3.7 and Tables 4, 6 report root contacts/distribution and dry mass partitioning toward reproductive organs in SDI 120, measured intermediate variables linking irrigation placement to yield. Q8: Conclusions state a potential shortcoming of SDI 120 with deficit irrigation in sandy soil (possible negative effects on reserve storage given leaf senescence, lower roots and trunk growth) and Discussion says the authors do not know whether SDI treatments lost fine roots after prolonged drying; abstract notes optimum conditions remain undefined. Q9: Table 5 gives yield means <U+00B1> standard errors for each treatment and year.
rows.notes: Yield measured only by harvest weighing (one method). Single vineyard, single cultivar, one soil; two seasons only. The yield difference was not explained by plant water status (similar predawn potentials); the authors attribute it to berry/cluster weight and partitioning, with root and leaf-area data as supporting intermediates. No explicit requirement conditions stated beyond general remarks that further studies are needed to define optimum conditions; the mention of Myburgh's contrasting result being due to table grape and high water application is about other work. Q4 'yes' is somewhat generous since soil water was measured in a parallel trial, not in this study.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a primary two-year field trial comparing surface and subsurface drip in a Sicilian vineyard and reports yield results directly relevant to the claim that SSDI yield effects vary across studies.
